content: Additionally, individuals on maintenance OST who receive psychosocial support are tracked to evaluate the integration of mental health services into addiction care. Community-based distribution of naloxone is provided at designated sites, and the quantity of naloxone distributed is recorded to assess the reach of overdose prevention efforts. Sites offering safe injecting equipment for gender affirmation purposes are also identified, as are those providing behavioral interventions aimed at reducing sexual risk and brief counseling for problematic substance use. Facilities offering tuberculosis (TB) prevention, screening, and management, as well as hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccination, are tracked to address co-infections in key populations. Sexual and reproductive health services are provided at specific sites, and the attendance of key populations at these services is monitored to assess their accessibility and utilization. Defined health sector intervention packages are delivered at specific sites, and tools are used to set and monitor targets for HIV prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care among key populations. Behavioral and sero-surveillance surveys are conducted periodically to gather prevalence data and understand the experiences, risks, and service utilization of key populations. These surveys must adhere to strict ethical research practices and involve the community in their design, implementation, and interpretation. Selection bias and sampling representativeness are critical considerations in these surveys, and methods like respondent-driven sampling may help reduce bias. Behavioral interventions for sexual risk reduction and substance use counseling are also tracked. Accessibility of interventions is assessed by asking key populations about their experiences, and mapping exercises identify where key populations live and congregate relative to service locations. Virtual spaces and online communities are increasingly recognized as important points of access for delivering information and interventions. Programmatic and administrative data, as well as key population surveys, are used to estimate coverage. Challenges include avoiding double counting and ensuring data disaggregation by population group. Unique identifier codes and recall methods are employed to improve data accuracy while maintaining confidentiality. Indicators such as the percentage of key populations provided with condoms and lubricants or the quantity of sterile injecting equipment distributed are used to assess program reach. Population size estimates are essential for calculating coverage indicators. These estimates must be relevant to the intervention of interest and consider the limitations of the methods used to derive them. For example, surveys of the general population may underestimate the prevalence of key populations due to stigma and underreporting. Indirect estimation methods, such as multiplier calculations and capture-recapture techniques, are valuable tools for deriving population size estimates. When reporting coverage indicators, it is important to acknowledge the limitations of the data and methods used. Integrated service delivery at single locations can enhance access to multiple interventions and facilitate coordinated case management. Sites providing multiple interventions are counted across relevant indicators, and efforts are made to identify locations offering comprehensive health sector packages.
